newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong paper hit by U.S. rate speculation.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong paper hit by U.S. rate speculation.

text.p: Hong Kong government paper gave up morning gains late on Tuesday on a Wall Street Journal report that the United States Federal Reserve might increase interest rates by up to 0.5 percent, dealers said.
The seven-year Exchange Fund note yielded 7.86 percent at the close, vitrually unchanged from Monday, after rallying to 7.80 at midday.
The five-year note yielded 7.50 percent, steady with Monday, after dipping to 7.40 earlier in the day. Three-year ended at 6.90 percent versus 6.87 percent the day before.
The one-week bill yielded 5.10 percent vs 5.03 at midday.
"There was impact from speculation that the Fed might increase interest rates by a half percentage point instead of the quarter point expected," a dealer with a Japanese bank said.
In the interbank market, however, demand and rates rose a shade on news of the U.S. attack on Iraq after President Saddam Hussein's incursion into the Kurdish city of Arbil over the weekend.
Overnight money was last traded at 5-3/4 percent against 5-7/15 3/8 percent on Monday, and three-month cash was last traded at 5-11/16 9/16 versus 5-8/19 19/32 percent.
